subject: MAP: Roles & timeline alignment for Nimbus Health evaluation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torrance <alex.torrance@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Roles & timeline alignment for Nimbus Health evaluation

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you over email. Per our phone conversation last week, I wanted to kick off a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align stakeholders, define success criteria, and lock a target close window for the pilot.

Quick intro of the Redwood team on this thread:
- Me (Sean) — your account lead for Nimbus Health. I’ll coordinate timelines, exec touchpoints, and commercial items.
- Dev Patel — Solutions Engineer (technical lead for the evaluation and integration).
- Maya Srinivasan — ML Engineer (evaluation design, metrics, and model comparisons).
- Marissa Cole — Solutions Manager (customer success contact; I looped her for the post-eval rollout plan).

Attached: Nimbus_MAP_v0.1.pdf (draft MAP with proposed milestones) and evaluation_checklist.xlsx (initial metric checklist).

High-level proposed timeline (flexible):
- Week 0 (this week): introductions + MAP signoff
- Week 1–2: environment prep (VPC, sample data exchange, access)
- Week 3: evaluation runs + initial quality baseline
- Week 4: tuning and cost/latency assessment
- Week 5: review & recommend next steps / SOW

Ask for Alex / Nimbus: can you please confirm the primary engineering contact(s) who will be hands-on for the evaluation and the preferred weeks for running the evaluation? Also, what are your must-have success metrics (latency SLO, acceptable error rates, throughput targets, or business KPIs)?

Two optional time windows for a 30-min kickoff call (PST):
- Tue 14 Sep, 10:00–10:30
- Wed 15 Sep, 14:00–14:30

If those don’t work, propose other times and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0103

Attachments: Nimbus_MAP_v0.1.pdf (13 KB), evaluation_checklist.xlsx (8 KB)

From: Alex Torrance <alex.torrance@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Roles & timeline alignment for Nimbus Health evaluation

Sean — thanks for the clear plan and the draft MAP.

I’m Alex, the Customer Engineering Lead at Nimbus. I’ll be the primary point for technical coordination from our side; I’ll also loop in Sarah Lee (integration lead) on implementation details — she’s CC’d. Our goals for the pilot are prioritized as:
1) model accuracy on de-identified transcripts (target F1 >= 0.82 for intent extraction)
2) end-to-end 95th percentile latency < 450ms for 1kB prompts
3) cost per 1k tokens under the threshold we discussed with procurement (I’ll share a target number in the contract thread).

We can do Tue 14 Sep at 10:00 PST for the kickoff. We’ll need a short pre-checklist for network/firewall items — our security team is strict about egress to hosted APIs. Can you indicate whether Redwood requires an outbound-only connection or if a VPC peering option is needed for the private deployment?

I’ve attached a short internal readiness checklist (for your reference).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
Alex Torrance
Customer Engineering Lead | Nimbus Health
alex.torrance@nimbushealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2201

Subject: Re: MAP: Roles & timeline alignment for Nimbus Health evaluation — technical kickoff agenda

Thanks Alex — joining Tue 14 Sep at 10:00 PST. Quick technical notes ahead of the call so we can be efficient:

Proposed 30-min agenda (kickoff)
- 0–5 min: participant intros & success criteria (confirm F1/latency/cost targets)
- 5–15 min: infra & data access (VPC options, sample de-identified data, ACLs)
- 15–25 min: evaluation plan & measurement (which model family to start with, quantization profile, batching targets)
- 25–30 min: next steps & immediate owners

Pre-kickoff ask (so we can provision quickly):
- A sample de-identified transcript set (~5–10k lines) — S3 link preferred (object-level ACLs or presigned URL OK)
- Network requirements: confirm if outbound-only egress to api.redwood.ai is acceptable, or if you require Private (VPC) deployment details for us to share (peering IP ranges, NAT, etc.)
- Any compliance paperwork needed before test data exchange (if so, point me to the contact and we’ll escalate).

Technical FYI: for the initial run we suggest a 4k-context configuration with the 1.7B/3B family as the baseline to get a fast cost/latency profile; Maya and I will run parallel evaluation traces (one tuned for latency, one for quality). We’ll share a short runbook post-call (redwood-eval-runbook.md).

If you prefer a private deployment for the evaluation, we can spin a dedicated trial in your VPC with a time-limited key; that path requires a slightly longer lead (2–3 business days) for network setup.

See you on Tue —
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0321

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Roles & timeline alignment for Nimbus Health evaluation — metrics note

Alex / team —

Quick note on metrics design from the ML side ahead of tomorrow’s call:
- Please confirm the labeling schema for the de-identified transcripts (intent labels and entity spans). If your schema differs we’ll map it but that adds time.
- For the quality run we’ll compute precision/recall/F1 and compare to your current baseline; please share the baseline numbers if available.
- For latency: we’ll report p50/p90/p95 with batching profiles for single-request and 16-concurrent-request loads.
- Canary plan: we propose running an A/B between a quantized model (int8) and the fp16 baseline to test cost/quality trade-offs.

If you can provide a small (200–500 sample) de-identified test file before the call, Maya and I can run a sanity pass and bring initial numbers to the meeting. If there are any constraints around the sample (format, columns, anonymization method), call them out and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — looking forward.
Maya Srinivasan
ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwood.com
